To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the plasma tumor markers of breast cancer, CEA and the CA15‐3 antigen, have a distinct kinetic response to the initiation of chemotherapy.

the tumor marker kinetics of breast cancer patients immediately after the initiation chemotherapy can be classified into four distinct patterns: 1) expected pattern: increase in tumor progression, decrease in tumor regression, 2) paradoxical pattern: acute surge in tumor regression, rapid and transient decline in tumor progression, 3) expected pattern: decrease in tumor regression and increase in tumor progression.
the plasma kinetics of tumor markers CEA and CA153 can be used to predict the clinical course of advanced breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of tumor markers in monitoring the clinical course and the therapeutic response in patients with advanced breast cancers.
the development of an early warning system for the detection of breast cancer and the prediction of the therapeutic outcome.
the development of new approaches in monitoring the clinical course and in predicting the response to chemotherapy in advanced breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of CEA or CA15‐3 for monitoring breast cancer is not recommended.
CEA and CA 15‐3 are useful in monitoring breast cancer patients.
the tumor markers, CCA and CA15‐ 3, can be used to monitor the clinical course of advanced breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma tumor marker kinetics are useful in monitoring the clinical course and in predicting the therapeutic response of breast cancer.
the kinetics of CEA and CA 15‐3 in the plasma of breast cancer patients are complex, and may be influenced by a number of factors.
CEA and CA 15‐3 kinetics can provide useful information in the management of patients with breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tumor marker kinetics can be used to predict response to therapy.
tumor markers are not static but dynamic and their changes can be interpreted in terms of tumor growth or regression.
tumor marker kinetics can be used as a prognostic marker for the clinical course of advanced breast cancer patients.
